title: Soveraeign issue metadata v1
description: Machine-readable contract for the YAML metadata block at the top of a Soveraeign GitHub issue.

actor_kind.description: Who tells the story, in the kernel's own attribution terms (SPEC.md actor_kind). A story is told by an actor, never by a system that has no expectations; a SYSTEM story is told on its behalf by the operator who integrated it.

asks.description: Extensions or adjustments the participant asks of the substrate, each addressed to the issue that owns it. A story with nothing to ask is a walked scenario, not a story.

blocked_transition.description: The exact transition that is unavailable: a STATUS.yaml gate, a SPEC.md kernel transition, or a ticket transition. A whole ticket, service, or session is never the value.

capability.description: Canonical capability identifiers this work item serves, from contracts/fixtures/capability-map.reference.json. A referent, never an identity: the ticket points at what the repository already names and never carries a second definition of it. Validated offline against the projection, because GitHub is a coordination surface and owns no product semantics (Bdo, Q6 2026-08-24; decisions/0053).

engagement_id.description: Identity of a verification engagement. A Red engagement is named for what it attacks, not for what it builds.

expected.description: What the participant expected to be able to do, in their words.

found.description: Where the realization fell short of that expectation.

governing_rule.description: The document and section that makes the precondition binding.

held.description: The ticket that cannot advance. It lists this unblock ticket in its own requires; blocked is never a status on it, only a held-by edge to here.

leans_on.description: Back-office supports the crossing cannot work without. Not a dispatch dependency: a story is never taken, so it never blocks and is never blocked.

missing_precondition.description: What the transition checks for and does not find.

reachable_alternative.description: The claim that no admissible path exists without the provision. Only the literal NONE is admitted: if an alternative exists, the held ticket is dependency-mapped, not blocked, and this ticket is refused (AGENTS.md, Blocked edge is not blocked frontier).

requested_by.description: The tier that found the transition unavailable.

requested_from.description: The tier asked to serve the provision. A judgement is always asked of the owner; nothing else may be.

requested_provision.description: What would satisfy the precondition. The type routes the ticket: a grant or judgement to the tier that holds it, a contract, fixture, capability, or observation to the tier that can produce it.

role.description: The participation or boundary role the actor holds while crossing (CLASSIFICATION.md). Owner is not a role: it is the context that sets an operator's Binding and Projection, and it travels in the ticket's authority field.

scenario.description: The conformance/scenarios.json id that walks this story. Null while the story is only told; required before standing may rise above PROPOSED.

story_id.description: Identity of a story: one participant crossing one counter and finding the substrate short.

target_head.description: The exact commit the engagement was run against. An engagement that does not pin its target cannot be reproduced.

target_pr.description: The pull request this engagement attempts to defeat.

unblock_condition.description: The observable condition that closes this ticket and makes the held ticket reachable again. A receipt, not a report, settles it.

unblock_id.description: Identity of an unblock request: one held ticket, one unavailable transition, one provision asked of a named tier.

stub_id.description: A verification engagement constructs nothing, so it carries no construction identity. An empty enum refuses the key outright rather than admitting it unchecked.
A story closes no repository surface, so it carries no construction identity.

bit_id.description: A story obliges nothing to exist; the counter it walks up to is the bit.

engagement_id.description: A story attacks nothing; it reports what a participant found.

requires.description: A story leans on supports; it is never dispatched, so it never requires. Refused outright so the dispatch DAG stays clean.

scenario.description: A story above PROPOSED must name the scenario that walks it; a told story cannot be bound, walked, or witnessed without one.

stub_id.description: An unblock request closes no repository surface; the provision it asks for may, under its own ticket.

bit_id.description: An unblock request obliges nothing to exist; it asks for what an existing obligation is missing.

story_id.description: An unblock request is not told from a counter; it is filed at a gate.

requires.description: If the provision is already some ticket's work, the held ticket requires that ticket directly and is dependency-mapped, not blocked. An unblock request exists only when no ticket will produce the provision, so it never requires.

requested_from.description: Judgement is owner-held; an unblock request for a judgement is addressed to the owner and to no one else.
